Require transition morphisms to be R-algebra maps so the R-structure on the colimit and flatness claim are defined.
Define K(x) as the subfield generated over k by the initial segment.
Use field-adjunction parentheses at both loci instead of polynomial-ring brackets.
Supply the least-element base case R'(x)=R and K'(x)=k before the nonleast limit construction.
Close the recursion by adjoining a greatest element and taking its ring, or explicitly take the final colimit and prove residue field K.
Prove the descended finite-etale algebra and all later base changes are local via faithfully flat descent/residue-algebra factors.
Repair the malformed Since/and clause and add the needed comma.
Change induction of the degree to induction on the degree.
Require a proper nontrivial intermediate field and repair then construction to then constructing.
Correct choicse to choices.
Change has at most cardinality to has cardinality at most.
Restrict the assertion to nonzero quotients because the zero ring is not local under the project's exactly-one-maximal-ideal convention.
Delete then from the malformed Given ..., then ... construction.
State that the uniformizer p is a prime number using an explicit copula.
Label the arrow as reduction modulo p^(n-1) followed by phi_(n-1), rather than the ill-typed bare phi_(n-1).
Name the respective source (x_i)-adic and target (y_i)-adic ideals in completeness and reduction.
Insert subring before R_0.
Replace the premature whole-lemma closure with This proves Case I; retain the existing final closure after Case II.
Split the footnote into explicit finite-generation and Noetherian-completion assertions so in this case has an unambiguous antecedent.
Insert the missing comma after K=L^G to make the invariant-subfield apposition grammatical.
State that the unique extension of D:R→R to the fraction field K satisfies D(a)≠0.
State that the difference lies in K and is integral over R, hence lies in R by normality.
Quantify over each finite purely inseparable L/K(x) and state that the integral closure of R[x] in L is finite over R[x].
Introduce R' with an explicit where-clause identifying it as the integral closure of R in L'.
Join the two Serre-criterion witness cases with or rather than and.
Repair the denote construction to denote this image by Z_(R').
Define the contracted prime, localize R' away from it, and use integrality plus normality in the common fraction field before the final localization equality.
After enlarging L, state that the original normalization is an R-submodule of the finite enlarged normalization and is finite because R is Noetherian.
